Logistics

Getting there, getting home

Point-to-point: Ride out of Grand Central, bike back to the city. No car required.

Start: Peekskill via Metro-North

The 7:55 am Hudson Line toward Beacon, from Grand Central or Harlem-125th St. Roll straight off the platform onto Route 202 along the river.

Aim to be at Grand Central by 7:30.

Finish: Strictly Bicycles, Fort Lee

A few of us will ride back from here to BK, but Strictly is official ride end.

The ride

Six chapters, north to south

We're climbing hard early while it's cool, then chill spin home along the water.

1
Mi 0 – 5.4

Peekskill to the Bear Mountain Bridge

Off the train and straight onto the Goat Path: Routes 202/6 carved into the bluff above the Hudson. It rolls upward with big river views almost immediately. The shoulder is narrow from mile 1.4, so ride single file and hold a steady line. Cross the Bear Mountain Bridge (take the walkway if traffic is heavy), then navigate the traffic circle on the far side with care.

Mi 1.4–5.4 · narrow shoulder Mi 5.4 · Bear Mtn circle
2
Mi 5.4 – 12.7

Perkins Memorial Drive

Quick bathroom stop at the Bear Mountain Inn, then climb Bear Mtn. Perkins Memorial Drive to the tower at roughly 1,305 feet, the high point of the day at mile 10.5. It comes early and it is long, so we'll take it cheeeeel and enjoy the view. The descent has hairpins: drops, brakes, space between riders.

Mi 6 · Bear Mtn Inn (water + bathrooms) Mi 10.5–12.7 · hairpin descent
3
Mi 12.7 – 27

The Harriman lakes

Off the Perkins descent and into the heart of Harriman: Seven Lakes Drive past the beaches, Tiorati Brook Road's wooded descent, Lake Welch Parkway, and the Kanawauke and Gate Hill roads. Two more summits in the 1,000 to 1,150 foot range live in here. Watch the pavement on Tiorati Brook Road, it's pothole country. Beach traffic on Seven Lakes can be heavy on a hot August Saturday. Water and restrooms at Lake Welch around mile 24.

Seven Lakes Dr · beach traffic Mi 18–21.8 · potholes Mi 24 · Lake Welch (water)
4
Mi 27 – 43

Down to the river

The long payoff: eight miles of net descent out of the park through Stony Point to the Hudson at sea level by mile 35. From there it's flat riverside riding into Haverstraw, where mile 40 offers an optional refuel before the gravel: a quick deli sandwich, or Big Daddy's Home BBQ if the group votes for a real lunch.

Mi 40 · Haverstraw deli or Big Daddy's BBQ
5
Mi 43 – 55

Hook Mountain gravel and the river villages

The route leaves the road for the Hook Mountain and Nyack Beach river trail: roughly three miles of gravel pinned between the Palisades cliffs and the water. The Haverstraw half is the rough half, rocky and steep in places with real cliff exposure, and walking the worst pitch is completely fine. It spits you out into Nyack for the lunch stop: the Runcible Spoon on North Broadway at mile 49.4, the classic cyclist bakery. Then an easy spin down to Piermont and its pier.

Mi 43–46 · loose gravel, cliff exposure Mi 49.4 · Runcible Spoon (lunch)
6
Mi 54 – 68.4

Sparkill, the 9W Market, and the ridge home

From Piermont through Sparkill onto the Rockland Road climb, about 450 feet back up to the Palisades ridge and the 9W Market in Palisades, NY: the classic last stop for food and bathrooms at mile 55.3. Then 9W south along the ridge, rolling between 400 and 500 feet with traffic that deserves respect, onto Hudson Terrace, past the George Washington Bridge, and into Strictly Bicycles for the finish-line espresso.

Mi 55.3 · 9W Market Mi 60–66 · 9W traffic GWB path entry Mi 68.4 · Strictly Bicycles

Study hall

Every. Single. Turn.

A wise SIG leader once decreed that a prepared rider studies every turn of the route on Google Street View before the ride. Who are we to argue. All 54 turns, in order, camera pointed the way we'll be riding.

Refuel

The stops

Six planned, roughly one every 90 minutes. Lake Welch is the last water in the park, lunch is Nyack or Haverstraw, and the 9W Market is the last food before the finish. We can skip any we feel like.

Plan B

Escape hatches

Turn back at the bridge

Mile ~5. If the legs or the weather say no, roll back down the Goat Path to Peekskill station. Trains run all day.

Skip Perkins

Mile ~8. Perkins Memorial Drive is a dead-end spur off Seven Lakes Drive that ends at the tower, so the bail-out is simply not turning: stay on Seven Lakes Drive and the group catches you on the far side. Saves about 5 miles and 900 feet of climbing.

Skip the gravel

Mile ~43. Stay on Broadway/9W from Haverstraw to Nyack instead of the river trail. Similar distance, all pavement, more traffic.

Bail to Tarrytown

Mile ~48 (South Nyack). The Cuomo Bridge shared-use path entrance is at 1200 Route 9W in South Nyack, inside Thruway Interchange 10, open 6 am to 10 pm. It's 3.6 miles across to the Tarrytown side (333 South Broadway), then about a mile to Tarrytown station and the Hudson Line home.

Ride notes

How we're riding it

Pacing Perkins

This is a medium-low spice ride. Bear comes at mile 8 with 60 miles still to go and we're going to take it chill. Settle in, spin, talk.

Gravel handling

28mm or wider tires are ideal for the Hook Mountain trail. Stay loose on the bars, and let the bike move under you. The Haverstraw half is rocky and steep; walking the worst pitch is fine and nobody will remember.

Descending

The two descents that matter are Perkins (hairpins) and Tiorati Brook Road (potholes). Ride both cautiously: hands in the drops, brake before the turn, leave space, and call out holes for the rider behind you.

Curriculum

Skills we'll be practicing

  1. Don't crash
  2. Don't blow up the ride
  3. Have fun
  4. Good vibes
